drafted_from: tool:google-account-search_mail's own row in tools/read-and-write-gmail/tool-rows.json (invoke method, url, body_template, input and output schema); Gmail response values worked out from that row for the synthetic input
start_here: Say to your AI: "Find mail from alex@example.com about the order. Use my Google account connection service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery." It runs tool:google-account-search_mail as that account and hands back the Gmail answer.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it calls Gmail for one Google account the connection names and answers what Gmail returns.
instructions: 1. Connect a Google account in your Workshop connections and note its handle, like service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery.

2. Say to your AI: "Find mail from alex@example.com about the order." and let it call run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:google-account-search_mail, and the input {"connection":{"connection_id":"service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery"},"query":"from:alex@example.com subject:order"}.
3. Read what comes back: the request goes as GET  the Gmail me-mailbox base (gmail.googleapis.com, v1)/messages?q=from%3Aalex%40example.com%20subject%3Aorder&maxResults=50&includeSpamTrash=true.
4. When nextPageToken comes back, run again with page_token set to it. Each id goes to read_mail_headers or read_a_mail.
